userStories.title: Flow start rows and availability
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the web pre-approval wire type and pure helpers for published feature rows and Start flow availability.

**Motivation** — Without them the flow is not usable from koda's web app, which is where a brainstorm thread publishes its spec set.

**Approach** — `ThreadDto` gains `preApproval: ThreadPreApproval | null`. New pure module `lib/fleet-flow-start.ts` with `FLOW_SPEC_PATH_RE`, `FlowStartRow`, `flowStartRows`, `FlowStartBlock` and `flowStartState`, as in Design. Tests in `tests/lib/fleet-flow-start.spec.ts`.

**Feature prefill.** `writtenPaths` is cleared by every publish (`thread-write-fold.ts`), so it cannot list the published specs. The rows come from the thread's own feature (`feature` + `specPath`) first, then each `.nax/features/<name>/spec.md` path in `lastWrite.paths` (only when `lastWrite.kind === 'published'`) whose `<name>` is not already a row, in path order. Specs published by an earlier publish are not listed; the user adds them as rows by hand. The API stays the authority on whether a spec path is real.

**Dependency prefill.** The design says to prefill dependencies from the design doc when it declares them; the web cannot read the doc's content, so each prefilled row after the first depends on the row before it (the safe default: no later feature starts before the earlier PR merges). The user edits them in the dialog.

Availability is visible only for a REPO thread with archivedAt null and canCreate true; when visible, notPublished (specPublished false or publishedSha null) precedes flowLive. Keep this module pure with no Vue imports. Add the required nullable web field without changing existing fields; update affected typed fixture constructors to preApproval: null if needed, preserving existing assertions.

**Scope** — In: web type mirror, row extraction/chaining/deduplication, ordered availability and unit tests. Out: role defaults and tickHint (US-002), form validation (US-003), dialog UI (US-006/007), permission reads and flow listing (US-008). API contract exclusions (not the required hand-written web ThreadDto mirror): Any API, DTO, OpenAPI or migration change; the thread entry and pre-approval routes are used as they are. Reading the design doc to prefill feature dependencies; prefilled rows depend on the row before them and the user edits them. Listing specs from publishes before the thread's last publish; the user adds those rows by hand.

**Interface** —
```typescript
interface ThreadPreApproval { userId: string; at: string; costCapUsd: string }
// ThreadDto gains: preApproval: ThreadPreApproval | null
const FLOW_SPEC_PATH_RE = /^\.nax\/features\/([^/]+)\/spec\.md$/
interface FlowStartRow { feature: string; specPath: string; dependsOn: string[] }
function flowStartRows(thread: ThreadDto): FlowStartRow[]
type FlowStartBlock = 'notPublished' | 'flowLive'
function flowStartState(thread: ThreadDto, opts: { canCreate: boolean; liveFlow: boolean }): { visible: boolean; enabled: boolean; reason: FlowStartBlock | null }
```
Export these declarations from their specified web modules.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] flowStartRows on a thread with feature: 'f-min', specPath: '.nax/features/f-min/spec.md' and lastWrite: null returns [{ feature: 'f-min', specPath: '.nax/features/f-min/spec.md', dependsOn: [] }].

[unit] flowStartRows on that thread with lastWrite of kind 'published' and paths ['.nax/features/f-min/spec.md', 'docs/design.md', '.nax/features/f-clamp/spec.md'] returns two rows, the second { feature: 'f-clamp', specPath: '.nax/features/f-clamp/spec.md', dependsOn: ['f-min'] }.

[unit] flowStartRows on a thread with own feature 'a' and published paths ['.nax/features/b/spec.md', '.nax/features/c/spec.md'] returns three rows whose third row is { feature: 'c', specPath: '.nax/features/c/spec.md', dependsOn: ['b'] }.
[unit] flowStartRows on a thread with own feature 'f-min' whose lastWrite.kind is 'discarded' returns only the thread's own row.
[unit] flowStartRows on a thread with feature: null and published paths ['.nax/features/x/spec.md'] returns [{ feature: 'x', specPath: '.nax/features/x/spec.md', dependsOn: [] }].
[unit] flowStartState on a REPO thread with archivedAt: null, specPublished: true, publishedSha: 'abc' and { canCreate: true, liveFlow: false } returns { visible: true, enabled: true, reason: null }.
[unit] flowStartState on a PROJECT thread returns visible: false.
[unit] flowStartState on a REPO thread with archivedAt set returns visible: false.
[unit] flowStartState with canCreate: false returns visible: false.
[unit] flowStartState on a visible thread with specPublished: false and liveFlow: true returns { visible: true, enabled: false, reason: 'notPublished' }.
[unit] flowStartState on a visible thread with specPublished: true and publishedSha: null returns { visible: true, enabled: false, reason: 'notPublished' }.
[unit] flowStartState on a visible published thread with liveFlow: true returns { visible: true, enabled: false, reason: 'flowLive' }.
[unit] flowStartRows on a thread with own feature 'f-min' whose lastWrite.kind is 'publish_failed' returns only the thread's own row.
[unit] flowStartRows on a thread with own feature 'a' and published paths ['.nax/features/b/spec.md', '.nax/features/b/spec.md'] returns two rows.

routing.reasoning: Small additive type/helper change, but availability includes an access-control permission check and requires the security isolation override.

modifiedFiles.reason: `ThreadDto` gains `preApproval: ThreadPreApproval | null` and the file exports the new `ThreadPreApproval` interface; existing fields are unchanged.

userStories.title: Flow start defaults and tick hint
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add pure role defaults and the advisory one-flow pre-approval coverage hint.

**Motivation** — Every fleet flow so far (flows 6 to 14) was started by hand with `curl` against the API, with a hand-written JSON body, and approved through a second API call.

**Approach** — New pure module `lib/fleet-flow-start-defaults.ts` with `defaultFlowRoles`, `TickHint` and `tickHint`, as in Design (outcomes checked in the order `none`, `notYours`, `exceeded`, `covers`). `tickHint` takes the `ThreadPreApproval` type US-001 adds. Tests in `tests/lib/fleet-flow-start-defaults.spec.ts`.

**Role defaults.** Both roles default to the thread's `backend.model` when the backend is `native` and has a model, else empty (the user types a model id). Role inputs are free text checked against the API's role pattern.

**Tick hint.** The dialog tells the user whether this flow will start without asking: the API's rule (`coversFlow`) is that the flow's creator is the tick's user or the thread's creator, and the tick's cap is at least the flow's cap. `tickHint` returns one of four outcomes, checked in this order: `none` (no tick), `notYours` (the viewer is neither the tick's user nor the thread's creator, whatever the cap), `exceeded` (the cap is above the tick's cap), `covers`. The hint is advisory; the API decides. When `useAuth().user` is null the viewer id is `''`, which no tick or thread creator matches.

`tickHint` compares caps as integers of ten-thousandths (`Math.round(x * 10000)`), never as raw floats. No Vue imports. The dialog computes isThreadCreator; this helper takes it as input and does not fetch auth or mutate a tick.

**Scope** — In: model fallback, ordered identity/cap hint, unit tests. Out: schema/role validation (US-003), hint translations/rendering and auth wiring (US-007/009), pre-approval mutations (US-005/011) and backend authorization changes. A model picker sourced from runner-advertised models for the role inputs; roles are free text.

**Interface** —
```typescript
function defaultFlowRoles(thread: ThreadDto): { reviewer: string; supervisor: string }
type TickHint = 'none' | 'notYours' | 'exceeded' | 'covers'
function tickHint(tick: ThreadPreApproval | null, costCapUsd: number, viewer: { userId: string; isThreadCreator: boolean }): TickHint
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] defaultFlowRoles on a thread whose backend is { kind: 'native', model: 'opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash' } returns { reviewer: 'opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash', supervisor: 'opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash' }.
[unit] defaultFlowRoles on a thread whose backend is { kind: 'native' } returns { reviewer: '', supervisor: '' }.
[unit] defaultFlowRoles on a thread whose backend kind is 'acp' with a model returns { reviewer: '', supervisor: '' }.
[unit] tickHint with a null tick, cap 3 and viewer { userId: 'u1', isThreadCreator: true } returns 'none'.
[unit] tickHint with tick { userId: 'u1', at: '2026-11-09T06:36:35.837Z', costCapUsd: '3.0000' }, cap 3 and viewer { userId: 'u1', isThreadCreator: false } returns 'covers'.
[unit] tickHint with tick { userId: 'u1', at: '2026-11-09T06:36:35.837Z', costCapUsd: '3.0000' }, cap 3.0001 and viewer { userId: 'u1', isThreadCreator: false } returns 'exceeded'.
[unit] tickHint with tick { userId: 'u1', at: '2026-11-09T06:36:35.837Z', costCapUsd: '0.3000' }, cap 0.1 + 0.2 and viewer { userId: 'u1', isThreadCreator: false } returns 'covers'.
[unit] tickHint with tick { userId: 'u1', at: '2026-11-09T06:36:35.837Z', costCapUsd: '3.0000' }, cap 3 and viewer { userId: 'u2', isThreadCreator: true } returns 'covers'.
[unit] tickHint with tick { userId: 'u1', at: '2026-11-09T06:36:35.837Z', costCapUsd: '3.0000' }, cap 3 and viewer { userId: 'u2', isThreadCreator: false } returns 'notYours'.

[unit] tickHint with tick { userId: 'u1', at: '2026-11-09T06:36:35.837Z', costCapUsd: '3.0000' }, cap 9 and viewer { userId: 'u2', isThreadCreator: false } returns 'notYours' (the viewer check comes before the cap).

routing.reasoning: One small pure helper module and its test need no new abstraction; the identity-sensitive coverage check still requires the security strategy override.

userStories.title: Flow start form schema
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add translation-aware zod schemas for the editable flow form and the pre-approval cap.

**Motivation** — Every fleet flow so far (flows 6 to 14) was started by hand with `curl` against the API, with a hand-written JSON body, and approved through a second API call.

**Approach** — New module `lib/fleet-flow-start-form.ts` with `FLOW_MAX_FEATURES`, `FLOW_COST_CAP_MAX_USD`, `FLOW_ROLE_RE`, `FLOW_SPEC_PATH_MAX`, `buildFlowStartSchema(t)`, `FlowStartFormValues` and `buildPreApprovalSchema(t)` (a `{ costCapUsd }` object with the same cap rule and the message key `fleet.flows.preapproval.validation`), mirroring `lib/thread-handoff-form.ts`. Issues are reported in schema order: rows top to bottom, then reviewer, supervisor, cap. The schema trims strings and coerces the cap as in Design; the duplicate-name and `dependsOn` checks are refinements on the `features` array. Validation messages are i18n keys under `fleet.flows.start.validation` and `fleet.flows.preapproval.validation`. Tests in `tests/lib/fleet-flow-start-form.spec.ts`.

**Feature names.** The schema also refuses a name containing `..` (as `fleet-dispatch.ts` does), although the API's `FEATURE_RE` alone would accept it: git refuses the branch `feat/<a..b>`.

**Form errors.** The form shows the first zod issue only, in schema order: rows (top to bottom), then reviewer, supervisor, cap. The duplicate-name and `dependsOn` checks are refinements on the `features` array (not the root object), so an invalid role or cap never hides them.

**Form values.** `FlowStartFormValues = { features: FlowStartRow[]; roles: { reviewer: string; supervisor: string }; costCapUsd: number | string }`. The schema trims feature names, spec paths and roles (`z.string().trim()`) before every other check, so duplicate and `dependsOn` checks compare trimmed names; it coerces the cap with `Number()` and checks at most four decimals as `Math.round(x * 10000) / 10000 === x`. `toFlowStartBody` takes the schema's parsed output and does not trim again.

API contract (unchanged): `POST /api/projects/:slug/threads/:id/flows` body `{ features: [{ feature, specPath, dependsOn?: string[] }] (1..20), roles: { reviewer, supervisor }, costCapUsd: number | string }`; features unique by name, `dependsOn` names only earlier features, `specPath` relative, ends `.md`, no `..`, at most 300 chars; roles match `/^[A-Za-z0-9._:/\x5b\x5d=,-]{1,200}$/`; `costCapUsd` > 0, <= 1000, at most 4 decimals. Mirror server-safe path constraints including rejecting NUL; the API remains authoritative.

Add fleet.flows.start.validation keys feature, featureDuplicate, specPath, dependsOn, featuresCount, role, costCap, and fleet.flows.preapproval.validation to both en.json and zh.json, preserving existing keys. Because this story has no dependency on US-001, keep its form row typing structural or otherwise avoid requiring a new unavailable runtime helper.

**Scope** — In: schema builders/constants/form-values type, English/Chinese validation copy, unit tests. Out: request-body conversion (US-004), field UI/error rendering (US-006/007), card submission (US-011). Any API, DTO, OpenAPI or migration change; the thread entry and pre-approval routes are used as they are. US-003 only: no acceptance criterion pins the 300-character spec path limit or a zero or negative flow cap; the schema enforces both and the API refuses them.

**Interface** —
```typescript
const FLOW_MAX_FEATURES = 20
const FLOW_COST_CAP_MAX_USD = 1000
const FLOW_ROLE_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9._:/\x5b\x5d=,-]{1,200}$/
const FLOW_SPEC_PATH_MAX = 300
type FlowStartFormValues = { features: FlowStartRow[]; roles: { reviewer: string; supervisor: string }; costCapUsd: number | string }
// Translation-injected zod builders, matching the existing handoff pattern:
// buildFlowStartSchema(t)
// buildPreApprovalSchema(t)
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] buildFlowStartSchema(t).safeParse succeeds on one row { feature: 'f-min', specPath: '.nax/features/f-min/spec.md', dependsOn: [] }, roles { reviewer: 'm', supervisor: 'm' } and cap 2.
[unit] On the feature name 'bad name', the parse's first issue message is fleet.flows.start.validation.feature.
[unit] On the feature name 'a..b', the parse's first issue message is fleet.flows.start.validation.feature.
[unit] On two rows both named 'f-min', the parse's first issue message is fleet.flows.start.validation.featureDuplicate.
[unit] On an empty row list, the parse's first issue message is fleet.flows.start.validation.featuresCount.
[unit] On 21 valid, distinct rows, the parse's first issue message is fleet.flows.start.validation.featuresCount.
[unit] On the spec path '/abs/spec.md', the parse's first issue message is fleet.flows.start.validation.specPath.
[unit] On the spec path 'docs/spec.txt', the parse's first issue message is fleet.flows.start.validation.specPath.
[unit] On the spec path 'docs/../spec.md', the parse's first issue message is fleet.flows.start.validation.specPath.
[unit] On a first row whose dependsOn is ['f-clamp'] while 'f-clamp' is the second row, the parse's first issue message is fleet.flows.start.validation.dependsOn.
[unit] On a row whose dependsOn is ['gone'] when no row is named 'gone', the parse's first issue message is fleet.flows.start.validation.dependsOn.
[unit] On the reviewer 'has space', the parse's first issue message is fleet.flows.start.validation.role.
[unit] On the cap 1000.0001, the parse's first issue message is fleet.flows.start.validation.costCap.

gains the same keys as the English locale file so the locale parity check stays green; existing keys are unchanged.

userStories.title: Flow start request body
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Convert parsed flow form values into an independent API request body.

**Motivation** — Every fleet flow so far (flows 6 to 14) was started by hand with `curl` against the API, with a hand-written JSON body, and approved through a second API call.

**Approach** — New module `lib/fleet-flow-start-body.ts` with `FlowStartBody` and `toFlowStartBody(values: FlowStartFormValues)` over the schema's parsed (already trimmed) output: it sends `costCapUsd` as a number and every row's `dependsOn` as a new array, without mutating its input. Tests in `tests/lib/fleet-flow-start-body.spec.ts`.

**Form values.** `FlowStartFormValues = { features: FlowStartRow[]; roles: { reviewer: string; supervisor: string }; costCapUsd: number | string }`. The schema trims feature names, spec paths and roles (`z.string().trim()`) before every other check, so duplicate and `dependsOn` checks compare trimmed names; it coerces the cap with `Number()` and checks at most four decimals as `Math.round(x * 10000) / 10000 === x`. `toFlowStartBody` takes the schema's parsed output and does not trim again.

Map features into a new array of request rows and copy each dependency array. Preserve parsed names, paths, roles and order; do not mutate source values or add transport fields. Accept the specified number|string form type, including number conversion for a string cap. Frozen valid parsed values must not trigger a mutation TypeError; this does not introduce validation or error semantics for malformed, unparsed inputs.

**Scope** — In: exported request-body interface, pure conversion and unit tests. Out: schema rules (US-003), network requests (US-005), defaults and UI editing (US-001/002/006/007).

**Interface** —
```typescript
interface FlowStartBody { features: { feature: string; specPath: string; dependsOn: string[] }[]; roles: { reviewer: string; supervisor: string }; costCapUsd: number }
function toFlowStartBody(values: FlowStartFormValues): FlowStartBody
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] toFlowStartBody on one row { feature: 'f-min', specPath: '.nax/features/f-min/spec.md', dependsOn: [] }, roles { reviewer: 'm', supervisor: 'm' } and cap 2 returns { features: [{ feature: 'f-min', specPath: '.nax/features/f-min/spec.md', dependsOn: [] }], roles: { reviewer: 'm', supervisor: 'm' }, costCapUsd: 2 }.
[unit] toFlowStartBody on parsed values whose cap is the string '2.5' returns costCapUsd as the number 2.5.
[unit] toFlowStartBody on a row whose dependsOn is ['f-min'] returns that row's dependsOn as a new array equal to ['f-min'] (the input array is not shared).
[unit] toFlowStartBody returns a features array that is not the input features array, leaving the input unchanged.
[unit] toFlowStartBody does not throw a mutation TypeError when valid parsed form values, their roles object, feature rows, features array and dependency arrays are frozen.

routing.reasoning: Single pure request mapper with a companion test, no new dependencies or stateful behavior.

userStories.title: Flow start and pre-approval composables
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose the existing thread flow-create and pre-approval routes through thin web composables.

**Motivation** — F1 (`fleet-flow-record`) built the thread entry route and the pre-approval routes, and F6 (`fleet-flow-page`) built the pages that read and act on an existing flow, but no screen creates a flow or sets the tick.

**Approach** — `useFleetFlows(slug)` gains `createFromThread(threadId, body: FlowStartBody)` posting (path built with `apiPath`) to `/projects/:slug/threads/:threadId/flows` and mapping the answer with the existing `write` helper. New composable `composables/useThreadPreApproval.ts` with `set` (PUT) and `clear` (DELETE) on `/projects/:slug/threads/:threadId/preapproval`, mapping an answer that carries `permissionKey` (`isPendingFlowAnswer`) to `{ kind: 'pending', request }` and any other answer to `{ kind: 'done' }`. Tests in `tests/composables/useFleetFlows.spec.ts` and `tests/composables/useThreadPreApproval.spec.ts`.

**Composable imports.** Components import `useFleetFlows` and `useThreadPreApproval` explicitly from `~/composables/...` (as `ThreadFlowsPanel.vue` does), because the Jest mount harness injects only its fixed auto-import list; tests supply them through the mount `alias`. Composable paths are built with `apiPath` (`lib/api-path.ts`), which the `api-path-guard` test enforces.

API contract (unchanged): `POST /api/projects/:slug/threads/:id/flows` body `{ features: [{ feature, specPath, dependsOn?: string[] }] (1..20), roles: { reviewer, supervisor }, costCapUsd: number | string }`. Answers 201 with `FleetFlowDto`, or the approval request summary when the route itself is gated. `PUT .../preapproval` body `{ costCapUsd }` (same cap rules) answers the `{ userId, at, costCapUsd }` tick; `DELETE .../preapproval` answers `{ cleared: true }`; both may answer an approval request summary instead.

Use useApi's existing base URL/envelope handling: pass /projects/... without adding /api. Do not catch/rewrite API errors in these composables. A FleetFlowDto in state PENDING maps to done, not pending; only a permissionKey summary maps to pending. Preserve list/get/overview/stop/answer and their existing tests unchanged except additive creation cases.

**Scope** — In: additive create method, set/clear composable, encoded paths, answer discrimination and unit tests. Out: component visibility and hint decisions (US-002/008/010), toast/navigation/reload orchestration (US-009/011). Any API, DTO, OpenAPI or migration change; the thread entry and pre-approval routes are used as they are.

**Interface** —
```typescript
// useFleetFlows(slug) also returns:
createFromThread(threadId: string, body: FlowStartBody): Promise<FlowWrite>
type PreApprovalWrite = { kind: 'done' } | { kind: 'pending'; request: ApprovalRequestSummary }
// useThreadPreApproval(slug) returns:
set(threadId: string, costCapUsd: number): Promise<PreApprovalWrite>
clear(threadId: string): Promise<PreApprovalWrite>
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] useFleetFlows('web').createFromThread('t1', body) calls $api.post with /projects/web/threads/t1/flows and exactly body.
[unit] createFromThread resolves { kind: 'done', flow } when the API answers a FleetFlowDto.
[unit] createFromThread resolves { kind: 'pending', request } when the API answers an object carrying permissionKey.
[unit] createFromThread rejects with the identical error object the API call rejected with.
[unit] createFromThread('a/b', body) calls $api.post with the path /projects/web/threads/a%2Fb/flows.
[unit] useThreadPreApproval('web').set('t1', 3) calls $api.put with /projects/web/threads/t1/preapproval and the body { costCapUsd: 3 }.
[unit] set resolves { kind: 'done' } when the API answers a tick { userId, at, costCapUsd }.
[unit] useThreadPreApproval('web').clear('t1') calls $api.delete with /projects/web/threads/t1/preapproval.
[unit] clear resolves { kind: 'done' } when the API answers { cleared: true }.
[unit] set resolves { kind: 'pending', request } when the API answers an object carrying permissionKey.
[unit] clear resolves { kind: 'pending', request } when the API answers an object carrying permissionKey.
[unit] set rejects with the identical error object the API call rejected with.
[unit] clear rejects with the identical error object the API call rejected with.

routing.reasoning: Thin standard HTTP wrappers, but they write approval authority and distinguish approval-gated responses; use strict security-path isolation.

modifiedFiles.reason: the returned object gains `createFromThread`; `list`, `get`, `overview`, `stop` and `answer` are unchanged.
gains the "createFromThread" cases; existing cases are unchanged.

userStories.title: Start flow dialog rows
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Create the dialog's editable, dependency-aware published feature rows.

**Motivation** — Without them the flow is not usable from koda's web app, which is where a brainstorm thread publishes its spec set.

**Approach** — New `components/fleet/threads/ThreadStartFlowDialog.vue` (Shadcn `Dialog`, vee-validate + zod with `buildFlowStartSchema`). Props: `open`, `thread: ThreadDetailDto`, `viewerId: string`; emits `update:open` and `submit`. On each open it fills the rows from `flowStartRows(thread)`. Each row has feature and spec path inputs, one native checkbox per earlier row's feature for `dependsOn`, and a remove button; an add-row button appends an empty row with no dependencies. Renaming a row rewrites that name in later rows' `dependsOn`; removing a row drops it from them. This story builds the rows part of the dialog; US-007 adds the roles, cap, hint and submit to the same component. Tests in `tests/components/thread-start-flow-dialog.spec.ts`.

**Dependencies follow renames.** Dependencies are stored by feature name, so renaming a row rewrites that name in every later row's `dependsOn`, and removing a row drops it from them.

**Checkboxes.** `components/ui/` has no Shadcn checkbox; the dependency checkboxes are native `<input type="checkbox">`, as `ApprovalPolicyDialog.vue` does.

**Feature prefill.** `writtenPaths` is cleared by every publish (`thread-write-fold.ts`), so it cannot list the published specs. The rows come from the thread's own feature (`feature` + `specPath`) first, then each `.nax/features/<name>/spec.md` path in `lastWrite.paths` (only when `lastWrite.kind === 'published'`) whose `<name>` is not already a row, in path order. Specs published by an earlier publish are not listed; the user adds them as rows by hand. The API stays the authority on whether a spec path is real.

**Dependency prefill.** The design says to prefill dependencies from the design doc when it declares them; the web cannot read the doc's content, so each prefilled row after the first depends on the row before it (the safe default: no later feature starts before the earlier PR merges). The user edits them in the dialog.

Consume the helpers assigned to US-001 and US-003 rather than reimplementing them; the binding dependency table leaves this story's dependency list unspecified, recorded as empty, so see the shared analysis scheduling warning. Reset on each opening (including an initially open mount), not on every edit/prop update. Closing forwards update:open false. Add fleet.flows.start row keys title, feature, specPath, dependsOn, addRow, removeRow to both locales without changing existing keys.

**Scope** — In: dialog shell, row initialization/editing, dependency checkboxes and reference maintenance, locale row labels and mount tests. Out: roles/cap/hint/submit implementation (US-007), networking and parent write state (US-009), helper/schema implementation (US-001/003). Reading the design doc to prefill feature dependencies; prefilled rows depend on the row before them and the user edits them. Listing specs from publishes before the thread's last publish; the user adds those rows by hand. Reordering feature rows by drag and drop; rows are added at the end and removed individually.

**Interface** — Props: `open`, `thread: ThreadDetailDto`, `viewerId: string`; emits `update:open` and `submit`. Consume `flowStartRows(thread: ThreadDto): FlowStartRow[]` and `buildFlowStartSchema(t)`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] Mounting ThreadStartFlowDialog open on a thread with own feature 'f-min' and a published .nax/features/f-clamp/spec.md renders two rows.
[unit] On that mount, row 2's feature input holds 'f-clamp'.
[unit] On that mount, row 2's spec path input holds '.nax/features/f-clamp/spec.md'.
[unit] On that mount, row 2's 'f-min' dependency checkbox is checked.
[unit] Row 1 renders no dependency checkboxes.
[unit] With three rows, row 3 renders exactly two dependency checkboxes.
[unit] With rows 'a', 'b', 'c', row 3's dependency checkboxes are labelled 'a' and 'b'.
[unit] Clicking the add-row button appends a row whose feature input is empty.
[unit] A row appended with the add-row button has no dependency checkbox checked.

userStories.title: Start flow dialog defaults, hint and submit
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Complete the dialog with model roles, cap defaults, tick coverage hint and validated body emission.

**Motivation** — Every fleet flow so far (flows 6 to 14) was started by hand with `curl` against the API, with a hand-written JSON body, and approved through a second API call.

**Approach** — `ThreadStartFlowDialog.vue` (created by US-006) gains the reviewer and supervisor inputs filled from `defaultFlowRoles(thread)`, the cap input filled with the tick's cap or `5`, and a hint rendering the `fleet.flows.start.tick.<outcome>` text for `tickHint(thread.preApproval, cap, { userId: viewerId, isThreadCreator: thread.createdById === viewerId })`. Submit validates with `buildFlowStartSchema`, shows the first issue's message in an alert (cleared on the next edit), and on success emits `submit` with `toFlowStartBody(values)`. Tests in `tests/components/thread-start-flow-dialog-submit.spec.ts`.

**Role defaults.** Both roles default to the thread's `backend.model` when the backend is `native` and has a model, else empty (the user types a model id). Role inputs are free text checked against the API's role pattern.

**Cap default.** The tick's cap when the thread has a tick, else 5 (the thread handoff default).

**Tick hint.** The dialog tells the user whether this flow will start without asking: the API's rule (`coversFlow`) is that the flow's creator is the tick's user or the thread's creator, and the tick's cap is at least the flow's cap. `tickHint` returns one of four outcomes, checked in this order: `none` (no tick), `notYours` (the viewer is neither the tick's user nor the thread's creator, whatever the cap), `exceeded` (the cap is above the tick's cap), `covers`. The hint is advisory; the API decides. When `useAuth().user` is null the viewer id is `''`, which no tick or thread creator matches.

**Form errors.** The form shows the first zod issue only, in schema order: rows (top to bottom), then reviewer, supervisor, cap. The duplicate-name and `dependsOn` checks are refinements on the `features` array (not the root object), so an invalid role or cap never hides them.

**Form values.** `FlowStartFormValues = { features: FlowStartRow[]; roles: { reviewer: string; supervisor: string }; costCapUsd: number | string }`. The schema trims feature names, spec paths and roles (`z.string().trim()`) before every other check, so duplicate and `dependsOn` checks compare trimmed names; it coerces the cap with `Number()` and checks at most four decimals as `Math.round(x * 10000) / 10000 === x`. `toFlowStartBody` takes the schema's parsed output and does not trim again.

On invalid feature/name duplication/spec path/dependency/role/cap, render the first issue under the form and emit nothing; HTTP orchestration belongs to the parent. Initialize roles and cap along with row reset on each open, displaying the numeric input as 3 for a '3.0000' tick. Add fleet.flows.start.reviewer, supervisor, costCap, submit, and tick.none/notYours/exceeded/covers in both locale files.

**Scope** — In: complete dialog inputs/defaults/hint, first-issue alert, edit-clearing behavior, parsed body emission, locale copy and mount tests. Out: row editing algorithms (US-006), pure helper/schema/mapper changes (US-001/002/003/004), HTTP/toasts/navigation (US-009). A model picker sourced from runner-advertised models for the role inputs; roles are free text.

**Interface** — Retain props `open`, `thread: ThreadDetailDto`, `viewerId: string` and emits `update:open` and `submit`; successful `submit` carries `FlowStartBody` returned by `toFlowStartBody(values: FlowStartFormValues): FlowStartBody` using parsed values.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the permission-aware Start flow entry control with publication and known-live-flow blocked reasons.

**Motivation** — F1 (`fleet-flow-record`) built the thread entry route and the pre-approval routes, and F6 (`fleet-flow-page`) built the pages that read and act on an existing flow, but no screen creates a flow or sets the tick.

**Approach** — New `components/fleet/threads/ThreadStartFlow.vue` (props `slug`, `thread`): reads `fleet.flow.create` and `fleet.flow.read` from `useProjectPermissions(slug)`, lists the thread's flows with `useFleetFlows(slug).list(1, thread.id)` (imported explicitly from `~/composables/useFleetFlows`, as `ThreadFlowsPanel.vue` does) when `fleet.flow.read` is held (re-checked on a late grant, as `ThreadFlowsPanel` does; a failed list counts as no live flow, with no toast), and renders the Start flow button and its blocked reason from `flowStartState` (`liveFlow` is true when a listed flow's state passes `isLiveFlow`). Tests in `tests/components/thread-start-flow.spec.ts`.

**Start flow availability.** Shown on a REPO thread that is not archived when the viewer holds `fleet.flow.create`. Disabled with a reason when the thread has no published spec (`specPublished` false or `publishedSha` null) or when the thread has a live flow (listed through `useFleetFlows().list(1, threadId)` when the viewer holds `fleet.flow.read`; without that key the check is skipped and the API's 409 is shown). Use the existing useFleetFlows list method; this story does not yet need createFromThread. Publication blockage takes precedence over a live flow through flowStartState. Do not impose thread-creator-only or session state restrictions, fetch without fleet.flow.read, toast read failures, paginate further or create a new stream. analysis:
Architecture and discovery: This is an additive enhancement to the existing human-facing web client, not greenfield work. Codebase-memory MCP tools are unavailable in this session, so discovery used direct source reads and text search at the supplied execution root. The automatically detected Next.js/Express labels in the prompt are inaccurate: apps/web/package.json:33 declares Nuxt 4.6.2 and apps/web/package.json:38 declares Vue 3; .nax/mono/apps/web/context.md:19 identifies Nuxt SSR with the existing root-level components/pages/composables layout. The API is the existing NestJS/Fastify system of record, not a new Express application. Implement only apps/web changes; do not change API DTOs, routes, Prisma, OpenAPI or generated clients. The phrase 'no DTO change' in feature exclusions refers to the API contract; the explicitly required hand-written web ThreadDto addition remains in scope. No database migration or client regeneration is needed.

Existing wire types and impact: apps/web/lib/thread-types.ts:141 defines ThreadDto, :183 extends it as ThreadDetailDto, :27 defines native/acp backends, and :121 defines lastWrite's discriminated union. ThreadDto currently ends with writtenPaths, publishedSha, specPublished and lastWrite, without preApproval. Add the required exported ThreadPreApproval interface and required nullable preApproval property without changing existing fields.
